A few of the orders which are germane to be noticed are orders dated 08-01-2024, 31-01-2024, 20-02-2024 and 27-02-2024 which read as under:
"08-01-2024:
This Court, on two occasions has granted time to the respondents to file his statement of objections.
The objections are not yet filed.
The issue is a refund of Rs.6 Crore 5 lakhs that is allegedly withheld by the Board.
Therefore, objections if any by the next date of hearing i.e., on 31.01.2024.

In the event, the Board would not file objections by then, it shall be construed that the Board has no objections to file to the petition and the petition would be heard on its merit.
List this matter on 31.01.2024 in Preliminary hearing."
--
31-01-2024

Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1, Sri. H.L. Pradeep Kumar on instructions would submit that the amount that has to be refunded to the petitioner after assessment would be refunded in its entirety before the expiry of two weeks.
List the matter on 20.02.2024 in the 'fresh matters list'.

In the event the respondent-Board would not refund the amount, the costs would ensue."

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the 1st respondent Sri.H.L.Pradeep Kumar submits that a demand draft for a sum of Rs.6,04,90,000/- is ready to be paid to the petitioner as a full and final settlement.
He would further submit that they have sought for the original receipts that are in possession of the petitioner.

Learned counsel for petitioner would submit that all the receipts that were in their end have been transmitted to the respondents and nothing is left with them.
In the light of the submission and the contra submission, list the matter on 27.02.2024 in the fresh matters list."
--
27-02-2024
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Advocate General representing the respondent - Board.

Learned Advocate General submits that the claim of the petitioner for refund of Rs.6,04,90,000/-
would be honoured and paid in the course of the day, by way of a demand draft.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the amount has to be refunded along with the interest, costs and damages as it is a case of unjust enrichment by the Board, who have kept Rs.6,04,90,000/- without refunding for 13 years now.

Learned Advocate General refuting the aforesaid submission contends that the Board was entitled to deduct 20% of the amount while making refund and it is not been done and 20% will also be assessed, if the interest aspect is considered.

Without causing prejudice to the rights of the petitioner upon the interest, costs and damages or the rights of the Board for deduction of 20% of the amount while refunding to the petitioners, the petitioners shall receive the total amount of Rs.6,04,90,000/-.
However, without prejudice as observed hereinabove.
Sri H.L.Pradeep Kumar, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1 hands over a demand draft bearing No.902203 dated 20.02.2024 and the learned counsel for petitioner acknowledges the same.
Learned counsel for petitioner submits an affidavit of the petitioner - company depicting that all the receipts that are at their end, are now handed over to respondent No.1 - Board.
There is no other receipt left with them.
The affidavit is taken on record.
List the matter on 27.03.2024, in the fresh matters list."
In terms of the aforesaid orders, the 1st respondent/Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board ('the Board' for short) has refunded an amount of `6,04,90,000/-.

Therefore, the issue of refund of the amount has since been redressed in view of the petitioner acknowledging it, what remains at this juncture is the claim of the petitioner Hassan Thermal Power Private Limited vs Karnataka Industrial Areas ... on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86110561/
4 for interest at 18% per annum as prayed for in one of the prayers quoted supra.

sentences.text: Therefore, the present petition is restricted to the consideration of grant of interest or otherwise.
The issue now boils down to narrow compass of awarding of interest.

3. Heard Sri R. K. Naroola, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Sri K. Shashikiran Shetty,
learned Advocate General appearing for respondent No.1 and Sri K.S. Rahul Cariappa, learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for respondent No.2.
4.
The petitioner being a Company in the generation of Thermal Power need not be gone into.
On 25-06-2007 a power purchase agreement was signed with the petitioner by the 2nd respondent/Government of Karnataka.
After signing of the power purchase agreement, the petitioner was directed to approach the 1st respondent/Board for allotment of land for the project in Hassan.
The petitioner thus makes an application to the Board along with the letter of the 2nd respondent/State Government, which had recommended allotment of 650 acres of land.

On 10-08-2010 the Board in its 302nd meeting resolved to allot 330 acres of land to the petitioner,
which had already been acquired by it for setting up of IIT at Hassan.
This was sought to be allotted to the petitioner as single unit complex.
The petitioner was directed to make deposit as was necessary.
The petitioner immediately deposits `5/- crores and `5/- lakhs on 13-09-2010.
Thereafter, in a meeting held on 02-02- 2011 the Board allots 320 acres as additional land adjacent to 330 acres of land that was earlier allotted.
On 05-08-2011 the Board revises the allotment made to the petitioner at 650 acres by reducing it to 450 acres.

On 20-09-2011 the deposit of `1/- (one)
crore was made by the petitioner as was directed.
Therefore, the petitioner all together had deposited `6/- crores and `5/- lakhs to the Board.

On 22-12-2011 the petitioner was directed by the Board to upgrade the capacity of the project from 500 MW to 600 MW pursuant to which the request for allotment of 605 acres instead of 450 acres was revived by the petitioner.

5. It is the contention of the petitioner that relying on the assurances given by the Board and the State, the petitioner had incurred huge expenses engaging international consultants for the purpose of setting up of the project and also securing environmental approval from the Ministry of Environment and Forest.
The expenses incurred by the petitioner are narrated in the petition.

The averment is, in the year 2015 the petitioner learns that Government has decided to withdraw the approval granted for setting of the plant and the agreement that was entered into between the parties.

Fearing cancellation of agreement, the petitioner in fact was at the doors of this court in Writ Petition Nos. 30351 of 2015, 30954 of 2016 and 41677 of 2017 all of which come to be disposed of by an order dated 07-01-2020.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The disposal was not on merits but on a memo being filed by the petitioner seeking withdrawal of writ petitions.
The prayer in the writ petitions was seeking approval and implementation of coal based thermal power plant at Hassan.
After withdrawal, comes the present petition seeking the afore-quoted prayers.
6. The issue now is, whether the petitioner would be entitled to interest at 18% per annum, so demanded, from the hands of the Board and compensation as is sought for.
It is not in dispute that a total amount of `6/ crores and 5/- lakhs is deposited with the Board in 2010-2011.
They were against certain allotments that were to be made.
The project did not take off.

The project did not take off not because of the folly on the part of the petitioner but did not take off because of the Hassan Thermal Power Private Limited vs Karnataka Industrial Areas ... on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86110561/
5 decision of the State Government.

sentences.text: Throughout these 13 years till the principal amount was refunded as noted hereinabove, the amount has been in the coffers of the Board.
If it had been in any Banking institution instead of it being in the coffers of the Board, it would have undoubtedly earned interest.

Therefore, the petitioner does become entitled to interest at Bank rates prevailing from 2010 till 2024 when the amount was refunded, notwithstanding the fact that the petitioner's claim is at 18%
per annum on the amount that was lying with the Board.
7. The learned Advocate General appearing for the Board would vehemently contend that under the allotment, the Board was entitled to deduct 20% while refunding.
The said 20% would amount to `1.3 crores.
The circumstances under which it can be deducted is altogether different than the circumstances that is prevailing in the case at hand.
If any default happens on account of the allottee it is then 20% can be deducted and not otherwise.
Here the project has not taken off not because of the petitioner but because of the administrative decisions of the State or the Board as the case would be.
Therefore, the petitioner's entitlement for interest on the amount that was with the Board for 13 long years sounds acceptance, failing which it would become enrichment on the part of the State.
The interest at 18% that is sought is ungrantable.
But, interest at bank rate from 2010 to 2024, the day on which the principal amount was refunded would become the period of calculation of interest by the respondent.
8. The other prayer that would remain to be considered is, grant of compensation.
The situations and circumstances in the decision making process that would emerge are myriad.
The claim for compound interest by the petitioner thus stands rejected.
Insofar as the claim for compensation is concerned, the petitioner is left with liberty to agitate its claim before the appropriate fora.
This Court finds the claim for compensation unentertainable.
The contentions advanced qua compensation shall remain open.

9. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) Writ petition is allowed in part.
(ii) The petitioner is held entitled to interest at bank rates prevailing in respective years from time to time from the date of initial deposit till the date it was returned to the petitioner.
(iii) The claim for compound interest stand rejected.
(iv) In the light of the observations made in the course of the order, the petitioner is reserved liberty to agitate his claim for compensation before any appropriate fora.
(v) All contentions qua compensation of both parties shall remain open.
